findings.correction_outcome: Specify ownership across the handoff: the injected runtime owns and settles every process, protocol and disposable state item until it successfully returns a session; after return the context owns and disposes that session. The factory maps failed/cancelled open to sanitized null-context outcomes, releases its session slot and disposes any session it actually received if later validation fails; the trusted caller always disposes its separate lease. Reconcile T010/T011/T018 tests with these observable duties and preserve zero real launches before T023.
findings.evidence: IPreparedJdtLsRuntime.OpenAsync returns an IPreparedJdtLsSession only after successful open. If it starts a process or protocol and then throws or is cancelled before returning, PreparedJavaNavigationContextFactory has no handle to those partial resources. The plan nevertheless assigns partial process/protocol/state settlement to the factory, and T010/T011/T018 require the factory to prove it. That cleanup obligation cannot be implemented or honestly tested through the documented callable interface.
findings.location: October Infrastructure construction seam, IPreparedJdtLsRuntime.OpenAsync and lifecycle paragraph; plan.md ID-S04

findings.affected_requirement: plan ID-I05 and ID-T04; spec FR-002 and FR-009
findings.correction_outcome: Keep T010 RED focused on the observable factory/profile/lease handoff, result mapping and lifecycle. Route real-runtime rootUri, disposable data/configuration and fixed restricted-setting assertions to an observable production-runtime seam and T022–T024 qualification, or first define an accepted settings projection if controlled testing of those values is required. Do not count fake initialization behavior as real JDT qualification.
findings.evidence: T010 asks a controlled injected runtime/session to verify the JDT rootUri, separate -data/configuration and fixed no-import/no-build/no-restore settings. The accepted runtime OpenAsync receives only the lease and profile, and the profile contains a disposable state root and bounds but no JDT initialization settings. A fake can verify factory handoff and raw-reply mapping, but cannot observe how the eventual real runtime constructs rootUri or JDT settings. As written, these assertions would mirror a fake or require an unaccepted production seam.
findings.location: T010 versus contracts/navigation-tool.md PreparedJavaNavigationProfile and IPreparedJdtLsRuntime.OpenAsync

raw_result.summary: Complete-definition REVISE. Prior P-PATH-TRUST-01 and T-PATH-LAUNCH-ORDER-01 remain resolved; plan review 06 accepted the new factory as within the existing 18.2 architecture. Current tasks reference the new design IDs and retain PATH-only selection, the closed real-launch boundary until T022/T023, 18.1's public read contract, 18.3's separate shared-lease ownership, and the fixture-first then prepared-Repository sequence. Read-only SpecKit analysis found two new semantic testability and cleanup issues. The feature prerequisite check passed and deterministic plan/task validation returned no errors, but it cannot detect P-PARTIAL-OPEN-OWNERSHIP-01 or T-RUNTIME-SETTINGS-SEAM-01. Real navigation and process protection remain unqualified. diff_sha256 is SHA-256 of canonical sorted path-to-artifact-SHA256 JSON encoded as UTF-8 with a terminal newline.
